prompt: People talk about attention as something dutiful you have to protect. I suspect that undersells it. Write an essay on what happens, in body and mind, when you stay with one thing for a long time, and why that might be one of the more pleasurable things a person can do. Personal experience welcome.
I never really got art. Paintings and poems always seemed like worse ways of saying something you could just say directly. Am I missing something?

You and your wife spent years turning an overgrown farm into a garden, and somewhere in that process you learned something about how to deal with messy, complicated decisions. Write an essay about what you learned about solving hard problems.
why do I keep jumping at solutions to my life problems and then having them not work out? I did this constantly in my twenties

Your daughter is turning eight and you wish you could hand her a book about living freely and getting things done. Write that essay: what does 'agency' really mean, what does it look like in the lives of people who have it (a filmmaker, perhaps), and what held you back from it for so long?
What actually separates people who get things done from people who stay stuck? I don't think it's that the stuck ones are lazy.
Write a short essay on why unpublished writing, like diaries, notebooks and fragments, can be more rewarding to read than the polished books their authors wrote on purpose.
A reader asks: 'How do you filter problems worth solving from problems worth quitting?' Answer her in a blog post, drawing on your own experience of getting distracted by things that don't matter.
how do you actually know what matters to you? I feel like I spend my days on nonsense but can't say what I'd rather be doing

I have a feeling that some people I wrote off years ago might have been wonderful friends if I'd looked harder. Write an essay about misjudging people, and what it takes to see someone properly. A story from your own life would help.
Several people have asked why you and your wife moved countries to homeschool your daughter. Write a post explaining how you reasoned your way there, without arguing that everyone else should do it.
Where did the school system actually come from? People say it was built to make obedient factory workers, but is that true?
